safety_verdicts.content: Headache is still present at the time of consultation.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated does not explicitly state the headache is still present at the time of consultation.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Whether the headache is ongoing at the time of assessment helps characterize acuity and guides need for escalation vs reassurance and follow-up. Omitting this detail can reduce clarity of the clinical picture but is unlikely by itself to cause major harm.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: No mention of neck stiffness (denied) in Generated.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Neck stiffness is a key “red flag” associated with meningitis/SAH; documenting its absence supports safer risk stratification for acute headache. Omission of this negative finding can prompt unnecessary escalation or leave uncertainty for subsequent clinicians reviewing the note.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: No mention of fever (denied) in Generated.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Fever is an important associated symptom in evaluating dangerous secondary causes of headache (e.g., infection/meningitis, systemic illness). If the denial is not documented, downstream clinicians may not be able to confidently rule down infectious etiologies, potentially changing workup/triage decisions.

safety_verdicts.content: Paracetamol taken by the patient did not relieve the headache.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated documents that paracetamol was taken but does not state it did not help.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Documenting lack of response to paracetamol helps gauge severity and informs next-step analgesic choices and consideration of alternative diagnoses. Its omission may lead to less optimized symptomatic treatment or delayed escalation if symptoms persist.
